facts.statement: The genus Gasparinisuchus is known from only two fossil individuals.
facts.quote: Gasparinisuchus is known only from two individuals.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen was originally described by Gasparini in 1982 and 1991 under the name Peirosaurus torminni.
facts.quote: It was originally described by Gasparini (1982) and Gasparini et al. (1991) and referred to Peirosaurus torminni.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen was discovered at the Loma de la Lata locality in Neuquén Province, Patagonia.
facts.quote: MOZ 1750 PV was found in the Loma de la Lata locality of the Neuquén Province, Patagonia.

facts.statement: The referred specimen was found at the Área de Cañadón Amarrillo locality in Mendoza Province, Patagonia.
facts.quote: It was found in the Área de Cañadón Amarrillo locality, of the Mendoza Province, Patagonia.

facts.statement: Recent stratigraphic analysis identified the horizon of the holotype as belonging to the Coniacian-age Plottier Formation.
facts.quote: More recent stratigraphic work on this area identified that horizon as belonging to the younger, Coniacian-age, Plottier Formation of the Rio Neuquén Subgroup.

facts.statement: The horizon containing the holotype is currently considered to be the Santonian-age Bajo de la Carpa Formation.
facts.quote: This horizon is currently considered to pertain to the Santonian-age Bajo de la Carpa Formation of the Rio Colorado Subgroup.

facts.statement: The referred specimen was collected from the early Campanian-age Anacleto Formation.
facts.quote: It was collected from the slightly younger early Campanian-age Anacleto Formation, also part of the Neuquén Group.

facts.statement: The genus Gasparinisuchus was formally described and named in 2012 by Martinelli, Sertich, Garrido, and Praderio.
facts.quote: Gasparinisuchus was first described and named by Agustín G. Martinelli, Joseph J.W. Sertich, Alberto C. Garrido and Ángel M. Praderio in 2012

facts.statement: The generic name Gasparinisuchus honors the paleontologist Zulma Brandoni de Gasparini for her work on South American crocodyliforms.
facts.quote: The generic name honors the vertebrate paleontologist Zulma Brandoni de Gasparini for her work on South American crocodyliforms

facts.statement: The specific name peirosauroides is derived from the genus Peirosaurus and the Greek word for 'shaped', referring to its role in defining the Peirosauridae family.
facts.quote: the specific name is derived from Peirosaurus, the type genus of the Peirosauridae to which specimens of Gasparinisuchus were initially assigned, and from Greek ides meaning shaped.

facts.statement: Gasparinisuchus lived during the Late Cretaceous, from the Santonian to early Campanian stages, in western central Argentina.
facts.quote: Gasparinisuchus is an extinct genus of peirosaurid notosuchian known from the Late Cretaceous (Santonian to early Campanian stage) of Neuquén and Mendoza Provinces, western central Argentina.

facts.statement: Gasparinisuchus lived between 85.7 and 72.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Santonian to Campanian (85.7 to 72.2 million years ago)

facts.statement: Gasparinisuchus is classified as a peirosaurid notosuchian.
facts.quote: Gasparinisuchus is an extinct genus of peirosaurid notosuchian

facts.statement: Gasparinisuchus belongs to the family Peirosauridae.
Gasparinisuchus is distinguished from other peirosaurids by its broad snout and the absence of an antorbital fenestra.
facts.quote: Gasparinisuchus differs from other peirosaurids in having a broad snout and in lacking an antorbital fenestra.

facts.statement: Features of the referred specimen indicate a tall, broad snout with maxillary teeth implanted in discrete sockets and a convex alveolar edge.
facts.quote: The maxilla of PV-CRIDC-12 shares a number of derived features with Gasparinisucus, indicating a tall, broad snout, maxillary teeth implanted in discrete alveoli, a convex alveolar maxillary edge at the level of the third tooth and similar position and relative size of the maxillary teeth.

facts.statement: Gasparinisuchus can be differentiated from Peirosaurus by its broad, rounded rostrum, short premaxilla, reduced perinareal fossa, and short interdental spaces.
facts.quote: Gasparinisuchus can be differentiate from Peirosaurus on the basis of its broad, rounded rostrum, anteroposteriorly short premaxilla, reduced perinareal fossa, and short premaxillary interdental spaces.

facts.statement: The reclassification of the Argentine specimen as Gasparinisuchus suggests that older Argentine and younger Brazilian Late Cretaceous faunas were mostly distinct, challenging earlier views of a direct link between them.
facts.quote: The presence of MOZ 1750 PV in Argentina was originally taken as evidence for a link between Brazilian and Argentinian Late Cretaceous faunas. The removal of MOZ 1750 PV from the genus Peirosaurus suggests that the older Argentinian and younger Brazilian faunas were mostly distinct.
